proposition: Install RentOK and the five headaches that knock a PG owner down every month can no longer touch him.

board.style_line: Handmade stop-motion diorama of an original side-scrolling platform game built inside a cutaway four-storey Indian paying-guest building: felt, clay and painted card, matte finishes, one large soft daylight source from the upper left (the building's window side) for the whole film, high key and bright, muted warm-grey and cream walls with grey-green damp patches, the only saturated colour is cyan #03FFF1 and it appears only on the power-up, deep blue #0038FF appears only on code-composited HUD grounds; 9:16 vertical frame, camera locked off and static unless the beat says otherwise, subject always facing or moving screen-right.
board.negative_line: No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no signage, no speech bubbles with words, no Nintendo or any known game character, no plumber outfit, no red cap, no overalls, no mushrooms, no question-mark blocks, no coins with symbols, no real brand marks, no watermarks, no extra limbs, no glossy plastic sheen, no hard black shadows, no camera shake.

identity_anchors.owner: A stout Indian man of about fifty, thick black moustache, short side-parted black hair, no cap, sky-blue and white checked half-sleeve shirt tucked into grey trousers, brown sandals, a large steel key-ring with a dozen keys clipped to his belt on the right hip; a felt-and-clay stop-motion figure with matte skin and round black eyes.
identity_anchors.phone: A plain black matte smartphone with rounded corners and no markings, held in the owner's right hand; its screen is dark until the cheat code beat and glows cyan #03FFF1 from then on.
identity_anchors.building: A cutaway dollhouse cross-section of a four-storey Indian paying-guest building: cream walls with grey-green damp patches, steel bunk beds with thin mattresses, a wall calendar with blank pages, one open stair at the right end of each floor, a flat roof with a black plastic water tank at left and a bare steel flagpole at right.
identity_anchors.verification_ghost: A tenant-shaped figure of plain grey felt with a smooth blank face and no features, holding a blank white card at chest height.
identity_anchors.rent_stack: A knee-high stack of crumpled off-white paper slips with a jagged torn-paper mouth, standing on two stubby paper feet.
identity_anchors.runaway_suitcase: A brown hard-shell suitcase with two running felt legs in black socks, dragging a white bedsheet behind it.
identity_anchors.ledger_octopus: A red cloth-bound ledger book lying open on the floor, spooling long strips of ruled paper like tentacles.
identity_anchors.complaint_tap: A brass tap on two thin brass legs spraying a fan of grey felt droplets, with a small brass hand-bell hopping beside it.

hero_frame.description: Fourth-floor landing, static medium-wide from the same side as the beat before: the owner stands at frame left, feet planted, right arm straight out toward frame right holding the phone like a blaster, the screen throwing a cyan glow across his moustache and shirt; a thin cyan outline traces his whole body; the grey water spray from the tap at the top of the stair hits that outline and turns to cyan dust in mid-air; the five monsters stacked on the stair to the roof lean back from him. The only copy in frame is the small HUD wordmark chip at top left.

audio.music_bed: An original marimba-and-soft-synth loop, minor key, low in the mix, entering only at beat 2 after the first hit has landed in silence; it drops one bass step on beat 5, stops dead on the third bell ring of beat 6, and returns at beat 8 in the major key one step faster; five ascending chimes on the kills in beat 9; one held chord under the flag and the brand card. No jingle, no sung line, nothing that resembles any known game theme.

beats.title: First hit
beats.feeling: Recognition with a wince: anyone who runs a PG knows this face on the first of the month.
beats.framing: Tight close-up, static camera. The owner's head and shoulders sit in the left zone, facing screen right. The rent_stack monster's torn-paper mouth enters from frame right and slaps his cheek; loose paper scraps drift upward; the keys on his belt jump at the bottom edge. Behind him a cream wall with a damp patch, soft and out of focus.
beats.first_frame: The owner's clay face fills the left two-thirds of the frame, eyes wide, one sweat bead on his temple, moustache lifted mid-flinch; at the right edge a fan of crumpled slips with paper teeth just touching his cheek; HUD strip along the top: the supplied RentOK wordmark on a small blue #0038FF chip at top left, four small key icons at top right as lives.
beats.impact: We cut in already mid-hit; the slap lands inside the first ten frames. Sound is a dry paper slap and one jingle of keys, no music yet. The shot holds the full 2.5 s so the face reads before the world is shown.

beats.title: Ground floor: who is this tenant
beats.feeling: Unease: a stranger at the door and no way to know who he is.
beats.framing: Static wide side view of the ground-floor cross-section. The owner runs in from frame left toward the front door at frame right. The verification_ghost fills the doorway holding its blank card; the owner skids to a stop and bounces back half a step; the ghost never moves. Code-composited nameplate 'TENANT VERIFICATION' sits above the ghost's head in the top-right zone on a dark grey chip.
beats.first_frame: Ground-floor cross-section: cream wall, a steel bunk bed at left, the front door at right; the grey faceless tenant fills the doorway holding a blank white card at chest height; the owner is entering at the far left edge mid-stride, keys swinging; HUD lives: four keys.
beats.impact: The owner's run is the movement that motivates the cut in; the stop is a flat felt thud. The music loop enters underneath here, minor key and low, after the emotion of the hit has been made in silence.

beats.title: Second floor: the rent that will not come
beats.feeling: Fatigue: the monthly chase from door to door.
beats.framing: Static wide of the second-floor cross-section with three closed room doors along the wall. The owner knocks on each door in turn moving right; each opens a crack, a rent_stack monster snaps its paper teeth at his hand and the door slams; felt coins spill from his shirt pocket toward frame left. Nameplate 'COLLECTING RENT' in the top-right zone.
beats.first_frame: Second floor, three closed doors, the owner's fist raised at the first door on the left, a paper mouth just visible in the door crack, one felt coin already in the air behind him; HUD lives: three keys.
beats.impact: Three knocks make the rhythm, three door slams answer them; the third slam is the cut point. Keys jingle on every knock.

beats.title: Third floor: gone with the deposit
beats.feeling: Disbelief: the tenant who leaves at night with the rent still owed.
beats.framing: Static wide of the third-floor cross-section, window open at frame right. The runaway_suitcase sprints from frame left past the owner, bedsheet trailing, and leaps out of the window; the owner lunges right and catches only the sheet. Nameplate 'LEFT WITHOUT PAYING' in the top-right zone. This is the film's one burr image.
beats.first_frame: Third floor, open window at right, the suitcase-with-legs mid-stride at centre with one leg raised, sheet streaming behind it, the owner at left with both arms reaching; HUD lives: two keys.
beats.impact: The suitcase's exit through the window is the movement that motivates the cut out. One soft whoosh, the sheet settling; the music holds without a swell. The exaggeration rests on a truth every PG owner has lived.

beats.title: Fourth floor: the register that never adds up
beats.feeling: Drowning in paper: money in, money out, nowhere it all lines up.
beats.framing: Static medium-wide of the fourth-floor cross-section. The ledger_octopus lies open at centre spooling ruled-paper strips that loop around the owner's ankles and wrists as he tries to step right; loose rent slips flutter upward. Nameplate 'NO RECONCILIATION' in the top-right zone.
beats.first_frame: Fourth floor, the red ledger open at centre with the first paper strip already looped around the owner's left ankle, the owner leaning right against it, slips in the air; HUD lives: two keys.
beats.impact: Paper rustle rising under the shot; the owner's strain motivates the cut. The music's bass drops one step, the level of light does not change: the mood is in the pose and the sound.

beats.title: Cornered: complaints from every side
beats.feeling: Overwhelm: one key left and every problem on the stair at once.
beats.framing: Static medium on the fourth-floor landing. The owner is backed into the left corner, hands up. The stair to the roof rises to frame right and is blocked, from the bottom step up: verification_ghost, rent_stack, runaway_suitcase, ledger_octopus, and at the top the complaint_tap spraying an arc of grey droplets over their heads down onto him while the bell hops and rings at his feet. Nameplate 'COMPLAINTS' in the top-right zone.
beats.first_frame: The owner pressed into the left corner, eyes shut, both hands raised; the five monsters stacked up the stair to the right with the tap at the top mid-spray, droplets frozen in the air; the bell at his feet; HUD: one key.
beats.impact: The bell rings three times; on the third ring the music stops dead and the frame holds in silence for the last half-second. This is the gap the film opens: how does he get past them?

beats.title: The cheat code
beats.feeling: A private grin: there is a way through, and he has it in his pocket.
beats.framing: Static close-up. The owner's right hand pulls the black matte phone from his shirt pocket into the centre of frame; the landing behind him dims to a graded-down grey. A code-composited pause panel appears in the upper zone on a blue #0038FF ground and the cheat code types itself one letter at a time in white: 'INSTALL', then 'RENTOK APP'. On the last letter the phone screen lights cyan #03FFF1 and the supplied wordmark composites onto the screen on its blue ground.
beats.first_frame: The owner's hand and the dark phone at centre, the dimmed grey landing behind, the pause panel above as an empty blue rectangle; HUD: one key.
beats.impact: Silence broken by one typewriter click per letter; then a single warm rising synth tone as the phone lights. This is the first cyan in the film, tied to the product here in close-up so it can be found small and fast in the wide shots that follow.

beats.title: Power-up
beats.feeling: Relief turning into swagger: nothing on that stair can reach him now.
beats.framing: Static medium-wide on the fourth-floor landing, same side and same setup as beat 6. The owner straightens; a thin cyan outline draws itself around his whole body; he raises the phone in his right fist at arm's length toward the stair like a blaster; the tap's spray hits the outline and turns to cyan dust in mid-air; the five monsters on the stair lean back.
beats.first_frame: The owner at left on the landing, phone held straight out toward frame right, screen glowing cyan, a thin cyan outline around his figure, grey droplets turning cyan where they touch it; the five monsters stacked up the stair leaning away; HUD: one key.
beats.impact: Hold the full 2.5 s so the transformation reads on its own. The music returns in the major key, one step faster; a soft continuous hum from the aura. The product is in his hand and in use; no copy is needed for the frame to sell.

beats.title: The run
beats.feeling: Momentum: every headache dissolving on contact.
beats.framing: The camera tilts up and tracks right, motivated by the owner's charge up the stair toward the roof. The phone fires short cyan bolts; each monster hit bursts into cyan dust and a small cyan felt tick-shape, in stair order: verification_ghost, rent_stack, runaway_suitcase, ledger_octopus, complaint_tap. As each falls, a code-composited super lands in the left zone and stays, stacking downward: '✓ DIGITAL KYC', '✓ AUTOPAY', '✓ DUES TRACKED LIVE', '✓ ONE DASHBOARD', '✓ COMPLAINT TICKETS'. HUD keys refill one per kill.
beats.first_frame: The owner at the foot of the stair at left-centre, phone out, the first cyan bolt frozen halfway to the faceless tenant on the lowest step, the other four monsters stacked up the stair to the right and above; HUD: one key.
beats.impact: Declared action passage: five hits on a steady beat of about 0.8 s, each a soft pop and a chime one note higher than the last. The supers stack and stay so the full list is readable for the final 1.5 s of the shot. The camera move ends as he reaches the roof hatch.

beats.title: The flag
beats.framing: Static wide of the rooftop against a pale morning sky: black water tank at left, bare flagpole at right. The owner runs in from the roof hatch at left, jumps and grabs the rope; a plain blue #0038FF felt flag rises to the top; he lands, hands on hips, keys settling. HUD: four keys. The five benefit supers fade out over the first half-second.
beats.first_frame: Rooftop, water tank left, flagpole right with the blue flag at half height and rising, the owner mid-jump with one hand on the rope; HUD: four keys.
beats.impact: The flag reaches the top with a soft cloth snap; the music resolves onto one held chord. Hold 2 s so the win reads, then a six-frame dissolve into the brand card.

beats.title: Brand close
beats.framing: Code-composed card on a flat blue #0038FF ground. The supplied wordmark (Rent in white, Ok in cyan #03FFF1) centred in the upper zone; 'INSTALL' and 'RENTOK APP' as two white bold lines in the centre zone; 'RENTOK.COM' in a smaller white line in the lower zone. Nothing else.
beats.first_frame: The card fully composed from its first frame; the only motion is the six-frame dissolve in from the flag shot.
beats.impact: The held chord decays under the card with a single soft click as it lands. Two seconds is the describe-aloud time for three short lines and the mark; the film ends on the pack.

hud_wordmark.why: Not a string: the supplied file rentok_wordmark composited untouched on a small blue #0038FF chip at top left of the HUD, inside the platform-safe area, so the brand is present from frame one and never lapses; four key icons at top right are the lives counter.

nameplate_verification.why: Game-style enemy nameplate above the faceless tenant, top-right zone, white bold on a dark grey #2A2A2A chip (measured 14.3:1); names the obstacle the way a game names a boss.

nameplate_rent.why: Same nameplate treatment, top-right zone, over the three doors.

nameplate_left.why: Same nameplate treatment, top-right zone, above the window the suitcase leaves through.

nameplate_reconciliation.why: Same nameplate treatment, top-right zone, above the ledger.

nameplate_complaints.why: Same nameplate treatment, top-right zone, above the tap at the top of the stair.

cheat_code_panel.why: The cheat code typed one letter at a time on a blue #0038FF pause panel in the upper zone, white bold (measured 7.0:1); the two lines stay on screen until the phone lights so a stranger reads the whole instruction.

benefit_stack.why: One line lands per kill, in the order the monsters fall, and each stays on so the finished list of five is readable for at least 1.5 s; left zone, white bold on dark grey #2A2A2A chips (14.3:1), stacked downward; fades out over the first half-second of the flag shot.

end_card.why: The ask, on the pack: wordmark upper zone, INSTALL / RENTOK APP centre zone in the largest type of the film, RENTOK.COM lower zone in the smallest; white on blue #0038FF measures 7.0:1 at every point of the flat ground.

mandatory.customer_words: The video has a Mario game. ... Game identity: An original Mario-inspired game, rather than an exact reproduction of Nintendo's character, artwork, music or game assets.
mandatory.realisation: An original stop-motion platformer: the level is a four-storey PG building climbed floor by floor, lives are the owner's own keys, enemies wear game nameplates, the win is a flag on the roof. No cap, no plumber, no overalls, no mushrooms, no blocks, no coins with symbols, and an original marimba loop instead of any known theme; the negative line forbids each of these in every prompt.

mandatory.customer_words: The player is basically a PG owner.
mandatory.realisation: The identity anchor 'owner': a fifty-year-old proprietor in a checked half-sleeve shirt with a dozen keys on his belt, present in every generated beat; the keys double as the lives counter.

mandatory.customer_words: The obstacles in the game are basically the problems that owner faces — tenant verification, collecting rent, tenants leaving without paying rent, no place to do reconciliation, solving complaints and so on.
mandatory.realisation: Five monsters, one per floor, beats 2 to 6, each carrying the supplied nameplate: faceless tenant (TENANT VERIFICATION), snapping receipt stack behind slamming doors (COLLECTING RENT), suitcase on legs out of the window (LEFT WITHOUT PAYING), ledger spooling paper (NO RECONCILIATION), spraying tap and ringing bell (COMPLAINTS). All five return together on the stair in beats 6, 8 and 9.

mandatory.customer_words: The game also introduces a cheat code — install RentOK app.
mandatory.realisation: Beat 7: the game pauses, the cheat code types itself as INSTALL then RENTOK APP on a blue panel, and on the last letter the phone screen lights with the RentOK wordmark. The same two strings return as the ask on the end card.

mandatory.customer_words: Once it is done, Mario gets a gun sort of power/immunity. ... Power-up design: Delegated to the creative system, while preserving the requested game-style power/immunity mechanic.
mandatory.realisation: Two halves of one power-up: the phone itself is held as a blaster firing cyan bolts (the gun), and a cyan outline around the owner turns anything that touches it to dust (the immunity). Shown first in beat 8 as the hero frame, then used in beat 9.

mandatory.customer_words: It runs and kills all the obstacles and gets the flag.
mandatory.realisation: Beat 9: he charges up the stair and takes out all five monsters in order, each kill answered by a benefit tick. Beat 10: he grabs the rope on the rooftop flagpole and the flag rises.

mandatory.customer_words: Platforms: Instagram Reels / Facebook and YouTube Shorts.
mandatory.realisation: 9:16 throughout; all composited text sits inside the central safe area (HUD below the top 10 percent, supers above the bottom 22 percent); the film passes the muted test because no meaning rides on sound.
Eleven contiguous beats, 0 to 30 s; the last is a 2 s code-composed brand close.

mandatory.customer_words: Brand and product source: Official RentOK website, https://rentok.com. Identity invariants: Rent in white, Ok in cyan #03FFF1, blue #0038FF ground.
mandatory.realisation: The supplied file rentok_wordmark is composited untouched, always on a blue #0038FF ground: HUD chip from 0 s, on the phone screen at 19.5 s, on the end card at 28 s. Cyan #03FFF1 is reserved for the power-up so the brand colour and the product's power are the same colour; blue #0038FF appears only under the mark and on the flag.

mandatory.customer_words: Visual treatment: Delegated to the creative system.
mandatory.realisation: Handmade stop-motion diorama in felt, clay and card; high key and bright as the game-comedy genre asks; one soft daylight source from the upper left held for every shot; matte finishes so the one saturated cyan reads as the only shine in the film.

mandatory.customer_words: exact_text_strings: INSTALL, RENTOK APP, TENANT VERIFICATION, COLLECTING RENT, LEFT WITHOUT PAYING, NO RECONCILIATION, COMPLAINTS, ✓ DIGITAL KYC, ✓ AUTOPAY, ✓ DUES TRACKED LIVE, ✓ ONE DASHBOARD, ✓ COMPLAINT TICKETS, INSTALL, RENTOK APP, RENTOK.COM (may_reflow false).
mandatory.realisation: All fifteen strings placed verbatim by code, none reflowed, none generated: five nameplates, one cheat panel, one benefit stack, one end card.

brand_timeline.in_context: HUD wordmark chip on every generated beat 0 to 28 s; the wordmark on the phone screen at 19.5 s inside the cheat-code close-up; the product in the owner's hand and in use 19.5 to 26 s; the wordmark on the end card 28 to 30 s. The brand is named on screen within the first second and the film ends on the pack.
brand_timeline.spoken: none: no dialogue or voice-over by production constraint; the brand name is carried by the composited mark and the end card only.

last_frame: Flat blue #0038FF card: the supplied RentOK wordmark in the upper zone, INSTALL and RENTOK APP as two white bold lines in the centre zone, RENTOK.COM small in the lower zone; nothing else in frame.

deviations.from: / / (ogx_0038): no cartoon for adults, no humour unless a brief clause asks; register interesting first.
deviations.brief_clause: 'The video has a Mario game ... An original Mario-inspired game' and 'Visual treatment: Delegated to the creative system' — the customer has specified a game-styled animated film; the comic exaggeration (suitcase on legs, tap on legs) is kept to the owner's real problems so the joke carries the selling point.

deviations.from: / / / (ogx_0042, abcd_0021, abcd_0012): supers equal spoken words, the CTA is voiced, the brand name is spoken.
deviations.brief_clause: The always-applying production constraint 'no dialogue or voice-over' plus the feed platforms named in the brief; the on-screen channel carries the ask and the brand alone, which is why muted_test is yes and every beat is legible without sound.

exact_text_strings are supplied in capitals with may_reflow false; each is at most three words on its own chip, set bold and large with measured contrast above 7:1, so the cost of capitals is paid with size and weight.

deviations.from: (whip_0046, hea_mts_0025): a borrowed fixed-meaning form is cliche unless re-angled; a template is a form, never the idea.
deviations.brief_clause: 'The video has a Mario game' — the platformer form is the customer's idea; the re-angle is that every obstacle is one specific PG-owner problem and the power-up is the product itself in his hand, so the form cannot be retold without RentOK.

deviations.from: / (ogx_0007, hea_mts_0016): a named individual and a hailing word in the opening line.
deviations.brief_clause: exact_text_strings are fixed with may_reflow false and contain no hailing word, and forbids an invented name; the buyer is hailed by the picture instead — the owner's keys, the PG building and the five problems flag a PG owner without a word.

deviations.from: / (abcd_0010): brand carried richly by more than one asset type including voice and music.
deviations.brief_clause: No voice-over by production constraint; the asset types used are the HUD mark, the product in use, the mark on the phone screen, the blue flag and the end card — no audio brand mention exists.
